metric.says: The number of people who visited your site. We are privacy-friendly so we don't use cookies and other persistent identifiers. If a person visits from multiple devices or on multiple days, they are counted as separate visitors. Within the same day, a person counts as one unique visitor even if they have multiple sessions.
metric.source: says: plausible.io/docs/metrics-definitions, Unique Visitors, less its closing link sentence. formula: lib/plausible/stats/sql/expression.ex:308-310 at plausible/analytics@b787d17, event_metric(:visitors), where ? is e.user_id.
metric.reads: A distinct count of `visitor` over the hits matching the window and the cursor. A visit-scoped slot matches a hit through its visit, so a hit carrying no source of its own still matches `source is google` when the visit it belongs to began on google. This DEPARTS from the sentence on every window longer than one local day: the vendor's `user_id` is a hash under a salt it rotates and discards inside 48 h (lib/plausible/session/salts.ex), so a person who returns on a later day is a second visitor to it and the same visitor here. The log can express the published reading — it is a distinct count of (visitor, local day) — and this app counts the person instead, so every multi-day `visitors` figure it shows is the smaller number.

metric.says: A session (also known as a visit) is a set of actions a user takes on your site. A visit starts when a visitor first lands on your page and ends when no action is taken for 30 minutes.
metric.source: says: plausible.io/docs/metrics-definitions, Total Visits (or Sessions), less its shopping-trip analogy. formula: expression.ex:450-452 at plausible/analytics@b787d17, session_metric(:visits), where ? is s.sign; at hour granularity the vendor smears instead, uniq(?) over s.session_id at :444-446. The 30 minutes of the sentence is NaiveDateTime.diff(event.timestamp, session.timestamp, :minute) <= 30 in lib/plausible/session/cache_store.ex.
metric.reads: A distinct count of the visits whose START instant falls in the window. Elixir's `:minute` diff truncates, so the boundary is the integer 1860 seconds and not 1800: 1859 s continues a visit, 1860 s opens a new one.

metric.says: The total number of times your pages were loaded by your visitors. A single visitor loading 5 pages counts as 5 pageviews but 1 unique visitor.
metric.source: says: plausible.io/docs/metrics-definitions, Total Pageviews, less its closing ratio sentence. formula: expression.ex:296-298 at plausible/analytics@b787d17, event_metric(:pageviews), where ? is e.name.
metric.reads: A count of the matching hits whose name is exactly `pageview`. This is not `pv_sum`: `pageviews` counts hits in the window while `pv_sum` sums the pageview counts of the visits that STARTED in it, and a visit straddling either edge belongs to exactly one of the two.

metric.says: The number of events (pageviews + custom events). When filtering by a goal, this metric corresponds to "Total Conversions" in the dashboard.
metric.source: says: plausible.io/docs/stats-api, the metrics table — the metric-definitions page publishes no sentence for this one. formula: expression.ex:302-304 at plausible/analytics@b787d17, event_metric(:events), where ? is e.name.
metric.reads: A count of every matching hit of any name but `engagement`, which is the tracker's own liveness ping and neither a page view nor a custom event. "Events count every hit" is a named wrong reading this oracle grades against: it answers 983 where this rule answers 751 on the (none, 28d) probe.

metric.says: Views per visit (also known as pages per session) shows the average number of pageviews per visit. Repeated views of a single page are included.
metric.source: says: plausible.io/docs/metrics-definitions, Views Per Visit. formula: expression.ex:482-491 at plausible/analytics@b787d17, session_metric(:views_per_visit), where the ?s are s.sign, s.pageviews and s.sign.
metric.reads: `pv_sum / sessions_n` to two decimals, with a zero divisor answering 0 rather than a NULL or a NaN. The numerator is each matching VISIT's own page-view count and not the window's `pageviews`, so the two disagree over any visit that straddles a window edge. The divisor is every matching visit — under a page filter it is NOT re-restricted, which is what makes it disagree with bounce rate.

metric.says: The percentage of visitors who land on a page and leave without meaningfully engaging with your site.
metric.source: says: plausible.io/docs/metrics-definitions, Bounce Rate, less its list of what counts as engagement and its benchmark ranges. formula: expression.ex:419-434 at plausible/analytics@b787d17, session_metric(:bounce_rate), where both ?s are the entry-page condition the dashboard's filter builds.
metric.reads: `bounce_n / bounce_denom` at a whole percent. A visit bounces iff it viewed at most one page AND carried no interactive hit that was not a page view. It is the only one of the three quotients whose divisor is conditional: under a page filter the divisor is rebuilt on ENTRY page, so a page nobody entered on gives visits above zero and a bounce rate of exactly zero.

metric.says: The amount of time visitors spend on your site. Visitors who only view one page are counted with a duration of 0 seconds rather than excluded. Average visit duration is the sum of all session lengths divided by the number of sessions, which includes those 0 second visits (bounces).
metric.source: says: plausible.io/docs/metrics-definitions, Visit Duration. formula: expression.ex:474-478 at plausible/analytics@b787d17, session_metric(:visit_duration).
metric.reads: `dur_sum / sessions_n` at whole seconds. A visit lasts from its first hit to its last NON-engagement hit, so a ping never extends it and a one-hit visit lasts zero seconds — and stays in the divisor.
